dedupe_keys.name: ebola cases and health system demand in liberia multi type branching process model data and code

description: This model estimates how many Ebola patients Liberia's health system would have to care for in the 2014 epidemic and which interventions would contain transmission. The producers are John Drake and colleagues at the University of Georgia, who published it with the PLOS Biology article Ebola cases and health system demand in Liberia. It is a multi-type branching process that separates transmission in the community, in hospitals and at funerals, with parameters that change over time to reflect behaviour change and interventions; ensembles are run over parameter sets that are both plausible and reproduce the observed epidemic, sampled by Latin hypercube. Coverage is national Liberia in 2014. The data and code are available as a free archive from Dryad, mirrored on Zenodo, under the CC0 dedication. Outputs include projected cases, the number of hospital beds needed and the share of cases due to hospital transmission. Caveats: fitted to early and incomplete 2014 case reports, it predates the epidemic's end, and the code needs familiarity with the article. Simulation uses: planning surge bed capacity and treatment centres during an epidemic, and testing how infection control in health facilities changes demand. Related records: the West Africa Ebola treatment centres (data-ebola-west-africa-treatment-centres-2014) list the facilities that were built, and Covasim (model-covasim) is a general epidemic model.
